properties.areaDesc: Barnstable; Nantucket
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 12 at 9:40AM EST until November 13 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.2 to 11.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Barnstable MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads
near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience
pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Splashover and very minor coastal flooding
are possible during the Friday afternoon high tide along north
facing beaches on Cape Cod Bay as well as Nantucket sound. No
significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor
coastal flooding will be quite short-lived, no more than an hour
on either side of high tide.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: McMullen, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 12 at 8:31AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below Cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Sunday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 15.0 feet
Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 12 at 5:19AM PST until November 17 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Widespread Moderate Impacts with total
snow accumulations up to 16 inches. Winds gusting as high as 50
mph.

* WHERE...San Joaquin River Canyon above 6,000 feet.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Friday evening and Monday morning
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. Motorists should use
extreme caution if travel is absolutely necessary.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne,
Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of
particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
